title: Test-run thread re-runs the compaction selection under StateInner on every 2 s tick after any revision change (~250 ms holds post-LOCK)
outcome: Whether the compaction selection pass and the test-run list handler should hold StateInner for about 250-360 ms on an active host is decided from measurement, and any fix reuses the existing projection-cut pattern from the scan path.
acceptance: Lock-hold cost is attributed by measurement: live rescan phase traces (test_runs.rs locked commit p50 about 290 ms at 1200+ live runs) and a live-population fixture split showing compact_test_runs_locked's full-history projection as the dominant locked sub-step, recorded on the item with run ids.

The compaction step no longer re-projects full history on an unrelated revision change, and the selection pass and list read make no per-row linear entry lookups or per-run wait scans. Deterministic count witnesses at two history sizes prove both, with the existing compaction suites green and a clean review pair, with no new cache, poller or StateInner field. Moving the remaining once-per-rescan selection off the lock is filed as its own item if still material after landing.
